1.title: How I deleted 95% of my agent skills and got better results — Nick Nisi, WorkOS
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Multi-agent orchestration with enforced state gates (verifier → reviewer → implementer loop) and cryptographic proof of work completion solves both context collapse and agent hallucination better than scaling a single agent.

2.title: When MVPs take 2 weeks but Prod takes 12 months — Jess Grogan-Avignon & Jack Wang, Accenture
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: Enterprise AI deployment bottleneck isn't technical (2-week MVP) but organizational — 12 months to production because security, governance, data, infrastructure teams operate in serial human-speed processes designed before AI's code velocity (1B commits/year, agents turning non-engineers into builders).

3.title: Why (Senior) Engineers Struggle to Build AI Agents — Philipp Schmid, Google DeepMind
3.author: AI Engineer
3.hook: Agent development is fundamentally iterative (prompt-observe-adjust) rather than deterministic (spec-code-deploy), requiring engineers to shift from "traffic controller" mindset (controlling every step) to "dispatcher" mindset (defining goals, letting the model choose paths).

4.title: Claude built a 3D home model from just a floorplan
4.author: How I AI
4.hook: Claude (via Cospace) inferred 3D structure and spatial reasoning from a 2D floorplan, then autonomously integrated external data (email furniture purchases) without explicit instruction — a concrete example of agentic UX reducing user friction.

5.title: Claude Opus 4.8: where it excels and where it falls short
5.author: How I AI
5.hook: Claude Opus 4.8 can autonomously code a full feature in one shot with correct architecture, but consistently fails on the same types of problems in the last 10%—the gap is not random but systematic.

6.title: Codex Goals enable the model to work autonomously for hours without supervision
6.author: How I AI
6.hook: Claude's /goal feature lets agentic systems work autonomously on unbounded problem spaces (e.g., "fix all errors in logs") rather than requiring task-by-task human orchestration, which changes both quality outcomes and the shape of agent UX.

7.title: How We Built Zeta2: Training an Edit Prediction Model in Production — Ben Kunkle, Zed
7.author: AI Engineer
7.hook: Zed's production training loop uses frontier model distillation + settled data filtering (running student checkpoints 50x instead of teacher 1M times) to generate high-signal training examples at scale, turning opt-in editor telemetry into self-improving datasets.

8.title: I let Codex run for 6 hours. Here’s what happened.
8.author: How I AI
8.hook: Goals in Claude Code enable multi-hour autonomous task loops by continuously working toward a measurable outcome (verify → decide next step → loop) rather than waiting for turn-by-turn prompts — the first time the author sustained a 5h45m uninterrupted agent run.

9.title: I Stopped Using PowerPoint After Building This Claude Code Skill (Full Tutorial + 3 Templates)
9.author: Peter Yang
9.hook: Claude Code skill that converts outline → animated HTML deck in minutes, with 12 templated slide formats, interactive charts, and QA pass via image rendering — showing a concrete pattern for AI-native tooling that replaces manual UI work.

10.title: No hype Claude Opus 4.8 review—my real experience
10.author: How I AI
10.hook: Opus 4.8 excels at one-shot feature building from spec but fails consistently on edge cases, bug-fixing loops, and hallucination under follow-up prompts—even on high effort mode.

1.title: Context Graphs for Explainable, Decision-Aware AI Agents — Andreas Kollegger & Zaid Zaim, Neo4j
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Context graphs add decision-making rules and policies on top of knowledge graphs, shifting agents from "what can you do" to "why should you do it" — using memory architectures (short-term conversation, long-term entity/org, reasoning) to make agents policy-aware.

2.title: How agent o11y differs from traditional o11y — Phil Hetzel, Braintrust
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: Agent observability requires measuring non-deterministic behavior (outcome quality, reasoning paths, token efficiency) rather than just uptime and latency — the building blocks are the same (metrics, traces, spans) but the scope fundamentally differs.

3.title: Reverse engineering a Viking VOIP phone protocol with Claude Code — Boris Starkov, Eleven Labs
3.author: AI Engineer
3.hook: Claude Code can reverse-engineer undocumented hardware protocols through iterative exploration (port scanning → command enumeration → brute force → state persistence debugging), turning a year-old unsolved problem into a working integration in days.

4.title: Run Frontier AI at Home — Alex Cheema, EXO Labs
4.author: AI Engineer
4.hook: EXO Labs is systematizing inference optimization across the full stack (models, software, hardware) to run frontier models locally—focusing on inference-specific hardware design rather than training-optimized chips, with early wins on Apple silicon quantization showing theoretical speedups not yet realized in practice.

5.title: Stop babysitting your agents... — Brandon Waselnuk, Unblocked
5.author: AI Engineer
5.hook: The gap in agentic systems isn't intelligence—it's context; a "context engine" that pulls both static organizational knowledge and runtime data at query time is what separates babysitting agents from autonomous ones.

6.title: The AI Skill I Rely On Daily — Priscila Andre de Oliveira, Sentry
6.author: AI Engineer
6.hook: Senior engineer at scale (Sentry, 100k orgs, 15+ years codebase, 100 PRs/day) stopped coding in Dec 2025 and now ships features via prompt-only workflow with Claude, treating code understanding (not code writing) as the bottleneck skill.

7.title: The maturity phases of running evals — Phil Hetzel, Braintrust
7.author: AI Engineer
7.hook: Evals mature through four discrete stages as agent complexity grows — starting from high-level failure modes (not exhaustive unit tests) and moving toward production observability as a continuous eval problem.

8.title: What the Best Agents Share — Mardu Swanepoel, Flinn AI
8.author: AI Engineer
8.hook: Four concrete agent UX patterns — focus modes (constrained action spaces), transparent execution (showing process not just results), personalization (injecting user context/principles), and one more — that shift from delegation to collaboration.

9.title: Why Rust is the Ideal Language for Vibe-Coding — Daniel Szoke, Sentry
9.author: AI Engineer
9.hook: Rust's strong type system and compile-time guarantees catch LLM errors that dynamic languages (Python, TypeScript, JS) miss because they're too flexible — making the language itself a guard rail against agentic mistakes, not the tests.

10.title: Why your agents need decision traces, not just documents — Zach Blumenfeld, Neo4j
10.author: AI Engineer
10.hook: Context graphs augment agent decision-making by storing decision traces, precedents, and causal chains alongside entity data—enabling agents to reason from "why past decisions were made" rather than just retrieving facts.
